subject: POC: model selection and quantization trade study for Acme Analytics

Subject: Post-call recap & proposed trade-study plan for Acme POC

Hi Tom / Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up infra: 

What we heard from your side:
- Primary goal: extract structured insights from customer support transcripts at ~100 qps peak, average 30 qps.
- Latency SLO: 150–250ms tail per request preferred (tight for large models).
- Priorities: 1) output accuracy / low hallucination on entity extraction, 2) cost control if quality impact is acceptable.

Initial model candidates we recommend for the POC (trade-off context in attached trade study):
- Llama-2-13B @ FP16 (baseline accuracy; highest cost, lower throughput)
- Llama-2-13B @ AWQ-4 (AWQ quantized 4-bit, big throughput gains, small quality delta on our evals)
- Vicuna-13B GPTQ (GPTQ path — sometimes better stability on instruction-following, slightly larger quality variance)
- Falcon-40B @ FP8 (high quality but heavier resource needs; include only if 13B-family shows regression)

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) You to send us the prompt set and 200–500 representative examples (thanks for the sample payloads today — please drop full set to the Drive link).
2) We will run a three-arm quantization trade study: FP16 baseline, AWQ-4 candidate, GPTQ candidate. We’ll report: P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, and quality metrics (entity F1, hallucination alerts) mapped to your prompt set.
3) Tentative schedule: baseline runs within 48 hours after we get the prompt set; full trade study results within 5 business days.

Attachments: quant_trade_study_AWQ_vs_GPTQ.pdf (short summary), acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (placeholder), latency_baseline_FP16.csv (example). Also linking our eval scripts: https://github.com/redwood/quant-eval-scripts and shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme-poc-benchmarks.

If this looks right I’ll get infra queued and book a follow-up slot for a live walkthrough of the results.

Thanks for the prompt set, Tom — good, representative samples. A few technical notes to set expectations for the trade study: 

- AWQ (our internal AWQ-4 builds) typically gives 2.5–3.5x throughput improvement over FP16 on 13B-class models with a 1–3% drop in micro-F1 on extraction tasks in our prior benchmarks. That delta narrows when prompt sets include strong anchors (explicit extraction instructions).
- GPTQ variants can have more variance: sometimes match AWQ in throughput, sometimes worse, and they can introduce tokenization edge cases that change decoding behavior (watch for entity boundary shifts).
- FP8 can be promising for larger models (Falcon-40B) but will require larger GPU instances and may push latency above your SLO for single-turn requests.

Proposed evaluation metrics (we’ll output a CSV per run):
- entity_precision, entity_recall, entity_f1
- hallucination_rate (heuristic: generated entity tokens not present in ground truth)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens_per_sec, cost_estimate_per_1M_tokens

Execution plan:
1) Baseline: FP16 Llama-2-13B on a single high-frequency instance; run against your 500-ex sample (will produce latency_baseline_FP16.csv).
2) Candidate A: AWQ-4 quantized Llama-2-13B.
3) Candidate B: GPTQ quantized Vicuna-13B variant (we’ll pin the model commit to avoid drift).
4) For each candidate we’ll run three repeats and produce per-run CSVs + a summary page (also include failure-mode buckets you requested).

I’m adding two links to internal run artifacts from a similar customer (anonymized) for reference: https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme-poc-benchmarks (we’ll add our new run outputs there) and our eval scripts: https://github.com/redwood/quant-eval-scripts.

Flag on quality regressions: if any quantized candidate drops entity_f1 by >5% absolute vs FP16, we recommend not using it for production; instead pick hybrid routing (FP16 for high-risk queries, AWQ for best-effort). We’ll call that out explicitly in the report.

I’ll start the baseline runs as soon as Aditya confirms and we have the Drive files in the folder.

—Marissa
